transforms: Read every program label in the 24 OpenSyria admissions catalogues (Open-Syria/website 0754506), which transcribe these announcements with announcement, page and row references.
Fold Arabic spelling variants and drop applicant quotas, campus suffixes, ordinals and gender notes, giving 744 distinct labels.

Assign each label to one field of study by its specialization, keeping technical-institute fields separate from degree fields where the qualification differs (for example Pharmacy Technology and Pharmacy).
Leave out military and security college labels, the medical preparatory year and faculty labels that name no program.
Keep the 30 existing field IDs and add 118 fields, each with an ISCED-F 2013 detailed code and a Ministry row reference.
Add Ministry spellings as aliases only when the alias maps back to the same field, and drop aliases shared by two fields.
Assign the 152 verified program offerings that had no field, using the award name before the shared Ministry row.
reviewNotes: Field names, English translations and ISCED-F codes were assigned by the maintainer from the Ministry labels and the UNESCO detailed field descriptions. Fields name what people studied; they do not assert that any university offers the program. Offerings still need their own award and campus evidence.
